traits.leaf_arrangement.note: APweb, Sapindales page, order characterisation (read 2026-10-16): leaves spiral. Opposite leaves in some Sapindaceae (Acer, Aesculus) and Rutaceae (Melicope and kin).

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: APweb, Sapindales page (read 2026-10-16): leaves spiral. Wikipedia, Burseraceae (read 2026-10-16): alternate and spiral.

traits.leaf_division.note: APweb, Sapindales page (read 2026-10-16): leaves odd-pinnate with opposite leaflets at order level. Wikipedia, Meliaceae (read 2026-10-16): usually pinnate.

traits.division_pattern.note: APweb, Sapindales page (read 2026-10-16): odd-pinnate leaves, leaflets opposite. Wikipedia, Burseraceae (read 2026-10-16): odd-pinnate, some trifoliate.

traits.rosette.note: APweb, Sapindales page (read 2026-10-16): mostly woody plants with leafy stems; no rosettes described.

traits.life_span.note: APweb, Sapindales page (read 2026-10-16): mostly woody; Biebersteinia a perennial herb; Nitrariaceae include herbs (Peganum perennial).

traits.inflorescence.note: APweb, Sapindales page (read 2026-10-16): inflorescences cymose; Sapindaceae paniculate. Wikipedia, Meliaceae (read 2026-10-16): panicles, cymes or spikes; Rutaceae: cymes or panicles. Branched cymose panicles drawn as panicle.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Wikipedia, Burseraceae (read 2026-10-16): flowers small and radial; APweb, Sapindales page (read 2026-10-16): monosymmetry only in parts of Sapindaceae (Aesculus and kin).

traits.zygomorphy.note: APweb, Sapindales page (read 2026-10-16): zygomorphic Sapindaceae and Rutaceae have unequal petals, not lipped or pea plans.

traits.corolla_shape.note: APweb, Sapindales page (read 2026-10-16): petals free (clawed in Biebersteinia), around an extrastaminal disc; shape inferred as spreading.

traits.hypanthium.note: APweb, Sapindales page (read 2026-10-16): a nectary disc inside or outside the stamens, not a floral cup.

traits.ovary_position.note: APweb, Sapindales page (read 2026-10-16): ovary superior throughout (stigma head of fused carpel tips above).

traits.carpels.note: APweb, Sapindales page (read 2026-10-16): Sapindaceae (2)3(-6), Nitrariaceae 3(4), Biebersteinia 5. Wikipedia, Burseraceae (read 2026-10-16): 3-5 connate.
